title: Proactive SLO oscillation mitigator for transient anomalies
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Problem: Our current automated rollback triggers react too quickly to short-lived spikes in latency/error-rate or transient token cost blips during canary and A/B rollouts. This causes unnecessary rollbacks and increased churn for model rollouts. Goal: Build a mitigation layer that reduces false-positive rollbacks by dampening oscillatory SLO signals while preserving timely automated evictions for true regressions. The solution should work across latency, error rate, token-cost-per-request, and throughput SLOs and integrate into the existing rollout controller.
background: We route canary traffic and run A/B experiments using the rollout controller. Existing triggers are threshold-based with simple windowing. During traffic spikes, noisy upstream telemetry and short-lived infra hiccups produce SLO excursions that briefly exceed thresholds, triggering auto-rollback. This ticket explores a hybrid statistical + policy layer (oscillation mitigator) to reduce spurious rollbacks without increasing mean time to detect real regressions.
design_overview: Key components: 1) Cohort-aware smoothing: compute per-cohort exponentially weighted moving averages (EWMA) with configurable alpha and a short-term volatility estimate. 2) Confidence-aware sequential test: use a sequential probability ratio test (SPRT) or Bayesian posterior probability to determine if the observed deviation is persistent vs. noisy. 3) Cost-normalized SLOs: normalize token-cost SLOs by request mix and payload size to avoid false alarms when cost per token naturally varies. 4) Hysteresis + graded action: implement multi-stage actions (alert -> throttle -> partial rollforward/rollback) with tunable hold windows. 5) Traffic-aware thresholds: scale sensitivity based on sample size/throughput (small cohorts require higher thresholds). 6) Explainability metadata: record the contributing signals and test statistics to surface to console and post-rollback diagnostics.
tradeoffs_and_decisions:
- EWMA vs fixed window averages: EWMA chosen for faster adaptation and smaller memory footprint; tune alpha per-signal.
- SPRT vs simple p-value: SPRT preferred for streaming detection with bounded error rates; will expose type-I/II configuration.
- Increased detection latency: expect 1-2 minute additional median detection time for noisy cases; acceptable given drop in false positives.
- Complexity vs observability: the mitigator will emit intermediate metrics to the Console to aid tuning; added complexity justified by operational savings.
acceptance_criteria: Integrates with rollout controller and can be enabled per-rollout via rollout.policy.mitigator = "oscillation".
False rollback rate (measured as rollbacks per 100 rollouts caused by transient anomalies) reduced by >= 60% on historical replay tests while true-regression recall remains >= 95%.
Expose tuning knobs in Console: EWMA alpha, SPRT thresholds (alpha/beta), minimum sample size, cost-normalization toggle.
Post-decision explainability payload attached to every automated rollback event (JSON blob) with contributing signals and SPRT posterior or likelihood ratio.
Unit tests for statistical detector, integration tests with rollout simulator, and end-to-end smoke test against staged canary in dedicated environment.
Documentation PR merged in docs/rollouts/oscillation-mitigator.md and sample config in templates/rollout.yaml.
Telemetry: new metrics emitted - mitigator.decisions, mitigator.false_positives_replayed, mitigator.latency_added_ms and dashboard created in Console.

implementation_notes:
- Use existing metric ingestion pipeline; add a lightweight stream processor node co-located with rollout decision service.
- Keep computation per-cohort O(1) memory using EWMA and a rolling variance estimate.
- Default configs: EWMA alpha=0.2 for latency, 0.15 for error-rate; SPRT type-I=0.01, type-II=0.05; min-samples=200 for throughput-sensitive thresholds.
- For low-volume cohorts (<200 samples/min) escalate to manual review rather than auto-rollback by default.
- Emit decision trace to tracing system with tag mitigator=true for easy correlation.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for EWMA and SPRT math with edge cases. 2) Synthetic traffic generator: produce transient spikes, sustained regressions, and mixed-cost workloads and run through mitigator vs current logic. 3) Replay historical canary traces from last 6 months and compare rollback counts and MTD (mean time to detect) tradeoffs. 4) Staged enable behind feature flag for 1% of rollouts, monitor mitigator.decisions and rollback rate for 1 week, then ramp to 10% then 100% if metrics in range.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: Unit + integration tests merged behind feature flag.
Phase 1: Enable mitigator in simulation mode (no action, just decisions) for 10% of rollouts and compare.
Phase 2: Enable graded action for low-risk cohorts (<=5% traffic) with manual notify.
Phase 3: Full enable with default hysteresis; monitor for 2 weeks and adjust SPRT params.
Rollback to old behavior via feature flag or per-rollout override.
observability: Metrics: mitigator.decisions{result=keep|rollback|throttle}, mitigator.likelihood_ratio, mitigator.ewma_{signal}, mitigator.volatility_{signal}, mitigator.latency_added_ms. Logs: decision trace with cohort, sample_count, test_statistic, reason_codes. Dashboard: prebuilt Console dashboard template id rollout-mitigator-2026.
